facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base at September 30, 2026 is one of strong reported profitability alongside heavy investment and rising leverage. Nine-month 2026 revenue is above the prior year because the average realised gold price is higher, while gold sold is lower (the release attributes the revenue increase to price, partly offset by volume), and Adjusted EBITDA is also higher. At the same time, cash capital spending, including capitalised interest, exceeds operating cash flow, so cash has fallen and debt has risen, partly through the Foran acquisition (debt assumed) and partly through revolver draws. The base is usable for a snapshot with these limits: trailing (LTM) EBITDA and so trailing leverage are not supplied because FY2025 full-year figures are absent; interest cover is shown on matched nine-month and quarter bases only; and covenant headroom cannot be computed because the covenant definitions and issuer-reported ratios are not supplied. The September 30, 2026 balance sheet also includes the Foran acquisition on a provisional fair-value basis, and Skouries and McIlvenna Bay are not yet in commercial production, so period earnings do not yet carry their full contribution while debt and interest do.

rows.label: Third quarter 2026 earnings are strong on higher gold prices, but capital spending far exceeds operating cash flow. Cash fell and debt rose sharply after the Foran acquisition. Leverage cannot be stated on a trailing basis.
Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow is well below capital spending, including capitalised interest, and company-defined free cash flow is negative.
Debt rose from the December 2025 level to the September 2026 level, driven by the revolver draw, the overrun facility draw and debt assumed with Foran.
Liquidity as cash plus undrawn revolver fell from December 2025 to September 2026, and a separate cash reserve for project loan repayments is excluded.
Debt maturities are spread, with the largest bucket in the third year, where the senior notes and revolver both fall due.
Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest several times over in each period computed, but the measure is company-defined and not the covenant definition.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Eldorado's business is a producing gold group with polymetallic by-products, now adding two copper-bearing mines through commissioning at the same time. Revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came mainly from gold, in three geographic segments, with Canada the largest after the Foran acquisition. The operating mines carry the credit today: Lamaque and Olympias improved, while Kisladag and Efemcukuru weakened on lower grades, and cost guidance was raised. The transaction that matters to a creditor is the all-share purchase of Foran, which closed on April 14, 2026: it added McIlvenna Bay and debt assumed of 355,321 (US$ thousand, recorded at fair value), mainly the Sprott facility, which is secured on the acquired assets with a company guarantee, plus an equipment facility. No new notes were issued in the period; new funding was revolver draws, the final overrun draw on the Skouries project loan and the acquired debt. Management describes Skouries as fully funded; that is a management claim, and the pack does not include a funding model. Skouries first concentrate was achieved on September 8, 2026 and McIlvenna Bay first copper concentrate in June 2026, but both commercial production dates are late in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the capital estimates and 2026 production guidance have moved adversely. Ownership, control rights and any shareholder agreements are not disclosed in the pack. Behaviour is assessed on documented actions only: a dividend programme was started and buybacks continued during the build, leadership changed on September 30, 2026, and no priming, drop-down or other creditor-adverse action is documented. Source evidence is primary and dated, so evidence quality is High for filed statements and Medium for management releases.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one transaction in the period is the acquisition of Foran Mining Corporation, completed on April 14, 2026 by court-approved plan of arrangement. The Q3 statements say the Company acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of Foran for 0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran share (Q3 statements page:8: "0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran common share"). Total consideration transferred was 2,394,995 (US$ thousand), of which share consideration was 2,385,625, cash 4,154, replacement option value 3,096 and the previously held equity interest 2,120; 64,668,321 shares were issued (Q3 statements pages:8, 17). The principal asset is the McIlvenna Bay project in Saskatchewan. The acquisition was therefore financed with equity, not debt, and the statements show net cash received on acquisition of 159,110 (Q3 statements page:3). Net assets acquired include property, plant and equipment of 2,696,191, goodwill of 446,181, debt assumed of 355,321 and a deferred tax liability of 501,024; the measurement is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year (Q3 statements pages:9, 10). Acquisition-related costs expensed in the nine months were 19.3 million (US$) (Q3 statements page:10). The Q1 statements disclose the completion as an event after the reporting date (Q1 statements page:22).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The debt assumed comprises the Sprott Credit Facility (a fully drawn 250 million non-revolving facility plus 44.9 million capitalised interest, maturing September 30, 2031, floating at 6.95% over the greater of three-month SOFR and 2.00%, secured by the realisable value of the acquired Foran assets and subject to a Company guarantee), the Sandvik Equipment Finance Facility (C$50.1 million outstanding, 60-month repayment) and repayable government contributions (Q3 statements pages:14, 15). Principal repayments on the Sprott facility start on June 30, 2027 at 2.65% of outstanding principal per quarter. Its terms mean the lender has a claim over the acquired assets ahead of unsecured creditors of the group on those assets, and the Company guarantee ties the facility to the parent; the pack does not include the credit agreement, so the full security and guarantee scope is Insufficient Information.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: realised price up from 3,527 to 4,326 per ounce (US$) while ounces sold fell and AISC rose (Q3 release pages:14, 15). Mechanic: revenue is carrying lower volumes at higher cost, so margin per ounce is more sensitive to the gold price than a year ago. Implication: debt service capacity rests on gold staying near current levels until the new mines add volume; the Skouries and McIlvenna Bay start-ups are the offset, and they are not yet in commercial production. Countering evidence: Lamaque output rose and Olympias costs per ounce fell (Q3 release pages:19, 21). 2. Cash conversion and refinancing. Evidence: acquired debt, revolver draws and a larger project capital estimate (Q3 statements page:14; Q3 release page:7). Mechanic: cash needs continue until commercial production, funded by the revolver and the cash balance; the Term Facility begins amortising on December 31, 2026 (Q3 statements page:13). Implication: refinancing and liquidity are the pressure points; the senior notes and the revolver both mature in the third year bucket (CP-1). Counter: equity paid for Foran and the revolver was extended to March 1, 2029. 3. Concentration. Evidence: Canada, Turkiye and Greece segments; Greece carries the Skouries project and the Term Facility secured on Skouries and Hellas Gold assets (Q3 statements pages:12, 16). Mechanic: the non-recourse project loan keeps Skouries debt away from the parent but ring-fences the cash flows of the Greek assets for that lender; the revolver and notes sit with the rest of the group. Implication: creditor claims on Greek cash flows differ by instrument; the pack does not contain the intercreditor terms, so recovery or ranking is not assessed. 4. Sponsor alignment and distributions. Evidence: dividends and buybacks during heavy spending (Q3 statements page:18). Mechanic: shareholder returns draw on the same cash as project funding. Implication: a monitoring point; no creditor-adverse action is documented. Counter: the Foran purchase was equity-funded. 5. Key uncertainties: commercial production timing and cost at both start-ups; covenant headroom (not supplied); ownership; Foran fair values (preliminary).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Eldorado Gold's credit view is cautiously constructive: profitable mines at high gold prices support debt, but debt is rising and cash falling while two new mines are commissioned. The strongest support is operating earnings and low illustrative leverage, financed partly by shares issued for Foran. The weakest point is nine-month free cash flow of USD negative 654.3 million and liquidity down from USD 976.0 million to USD 671.5 million since December 2025. The outcome depends on Skouries and McIlvenna Bay reaching commercial production in late Q4 2026 at or near the revised budgets, on gold prices holding, and on the senior notes and revolver refinancing from 2029. Confidence is Medium because trailing earnings and covenant headroom are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Eldorado Gold's cash is being consumed by growth spending rather than by operations. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 it generated USD 425.7 million of operating cash flow from continuing operations but spent USD 1,210.0 million on property, plant and equipment and USD 45.9 million on capitalised interest paid, a shortfall of about USD 830.2 million before acquisition cash, dividends, buybacks and borrowings (CP-1, Calculations). Company-defined free cash flow was negative USD 654.3 million; excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay it was positive USD 202.1 million (Q3 release page:13). Mechanic: the operating mines are cash generative and the two projects absorb it, so default risk is driven by project completion, not by the operating base. Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 2. Liquidity has fallen but covers near-term maturities. Unrestricted cash was USD 396.8 million and the undrawn revolver USD 274.7 million at September 30, 2026, together USD 671.5 million against USD 976.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1). Principal falling due within a year is USD 141.1 million, so liquidity is about 4.8 times that amount (Calculations). Restricted cash of USD 71.9 million for the Skouries term loan reserve and the undrawn euro 30 million VAT facility are excluded. Mechanic: the cushion is adequate for scheduled repayments but not for a prolonged slip in the start-ups combined with a lower gold price. Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 3. Debt rose by USD 710.4 million to USD 1,985.4 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (carrying amount). The increase came from USD 321.6 million of revolver borrowings, USD 68.1 million from the final overrun draw on the Skouries loan, and USD 350.5 million of Foran-related debt (the Sprott facility net of its redemption option derivative asset, the equipment facility and government contributions), partly offset by repayments and movements on the Skouries project loans and the VAT facility (CP-1 debt table; Calculations). Foran itself was paid for with shares (USD 2,385.6 million of share consideration), which kept the acquisition from adding to leverage through the purchase price (CP-1A). Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 4. Reported leverage looks moderate only on an illustrative basis. Total debt to annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is 1.67 times and net debt to the same measure 1.34 times; neither is a trailing twelve-month figure because FY2025 EBITDA is not supplied, and the base includes Foran only from April 14, 2026 and no Skouries contribution (CP-1). Cash interest cover (Adjusted EBITDA over interest paid plus capitalised interest paid) was 11.96 times for nine months 2026 and 9.81 times for Q3 2026. These do not use the covenant definitions, so headroom against the revolver tests of at least 3.00 times interest cover and at most 3.50 times net leverage is Not calculable. The illustrative figures sit well inside those levels, which is a reading and not a compliance finding; the Company states it complied at September 30, 2026 (Q3 statements page:14). Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 5. Skouries and McIlvenna Bay execution is the pivotal risk. First concentrate was reached at Skouries on September 8, 2026 and at McIlvenna Bay in June 2026, with commercial production for both expected late in Q4 2026 (CP-1A). The Skouries project capital estimate rose from about USD 1.315 billion in the Q1 release to about USD 1.425 billion, the McIlvenna Bay estimate from USD 952 million in the Q2 release to USD 975 million, and the 2026 production outlook was cut to 425,000 to 475,000 ounces from 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. On the release's own figures, remaining Skouries project capital is about USD 46 million and accelerated operational capital about USD 104 million, with up to USD 30 million more possible (Calculations); the remaining McIlvenna Bay spend is Not calculable because spending before the acquisition date is not in the pack. Mechanic: further slippage extends the period of negative free cash flow and delays the debt reduction that management says it expects. Management Language on funding ("fully funded") is not adopted because no funding model is supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 6. Refinancing is concentrated and amortisation starts soon. Principal due by year after September 30, 2026 is USD 141.1 million, 142.5 million, 958.8 million, 162.4 million, 354.7 million and 258.2 million beyond year five (CP-1). The third year contains the USD 500.0 million 6.25% senior notes due September 1, 2029 and the USD 325.0 million revolver drawn to March 1, 2029, the largest bucket by a wide margin. The Skouries term loan, non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries and Hellas Gold assets, begins repaying on December 31, 2026 in 13 semi-annual instalments (Q3 statements page:13). Mechanic: if the start-ups deliver, cash flow and the equity-funded balance sheet should support refinancing; if not, the 2029 wall arrives with higher debt. Documentary Fact for the schedule, Analyst Interpretation for the refinancing reading.

facts.text: 7. Shareholder returns continued during the build. Dividends of USD 54.1 million and cancelled buybacks of USD 83.9 million in nine months 2026, about USD 138.0 million together, were paid while free cash flow was negative (CP-1A, Calculations). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company reports compliance. No creditor-adverse action is documented. Mechanic: these returns draw on the same liquidity that funds the projects and can be reduced by the board; they are a monitoring point, not a finding of extraction. Analyst Interpretation.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 8. Earnings quality needs care. Net earnings from continuing operations were USD 426.2 million for nine months 2026 against USD 270.0 million a year earlier, but the 2025 period included a deferred tax recovery of USD 89.4 million and the 2026 effective tax rate was 37.6% against 16.8% (CP-1 Calculations). The Adjusted EBITDA measure of USD 892.0 million adds back a USD 97.6 million realised loss on gold and copper derivatives and USD 21.3 million of acquisition costs, and removes a USD 100.6 million unrealised derivative gain (Q3 release page:24). Mechanic: the realised swap loss is a real cost of the Skouries financing hedges that the adjusted figure leaves out; those swaps have expired with financial settlement (Q3 statements page:22), so the item should not recur, but the adjusted measure is higher than the unadjusted result for 2026. Documentary Fact.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, the operating base earns at high gold prices: the average realised gold price was USD 4,326 per ounce in Q3 2026 against USD 3,527 a year earlier, and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 892.0 million against USD 571.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1). Second, diversification across Turkiye, Canada and Greece with Canada now the largest segment at about 45% of nine-month revenue, and several mines at different cost levels, with Lamaque cash costs of USD 897 per ounce in Q3 2026 (CP-1A, Calculations; Analyst Interpretation). Third, an equity-funded Foran purchase that added roughly 24.7% to shares outstanding rather than debt to fund the price, and an extended and enlarged revolver of USD 600.0 million maturing March 1, 2029 (Documentary Fact). Fourth, a Skouries project loan that the notes describe as non-recourse to Eldorado Gold Corporation, which limits parent exposure to that lender if the project falls short (Documentary Fact for the description; the legal documents are not supplied, so the extent of recourse is not verified). Fifth, interest cover on cash interest of about ten to twelve times on matched bases (Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. First, negative free cash flow and falling liquidity, with debt up USD 710.4 million in nine months (Documentary Fact). Second, cost and guidance deterioration: all-in sustaining cost guidance raised and 2026 production outlook cut, with Kisladag and Olympias weaker (Documentary Fact). Third, start-up risk and rising project capital at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, with commercial production dates still forward-looking (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Fourth, a concentrated maturity profile and the start of Skouries term loan repayments in December 2026 (Documentary Fact). Fifth, a leadership transition on September 30, 2026 during the overrun period and shareholder distributions during the build (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the credit effect). Sixth, high effective tax in 2026 and exposure to a high gold price: the earnings strength depends on a gold price the company does not control, and the pack contains no sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation; sensitivity Not supplied).

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Nine-month 2026 cash shortfall after capital spending (US$ thousand): 425,747 operating cash flow less 1,210,017 property, plant and equipment additions less 45,943 capitalised interest paid equals negative 830,213 (inputs from CP-1; checked to Q3 statements pages:3). It excludes the 159,110 of cash received on the Foran acquisition, dividends, buybacks and borrowings. 2. Liquidity cover of year-one maturities (US$m): cash 396.828 plus undrawn revolver 274.7 equals 671.528; divided by principal due within one year 141.053 equals 4.76 times. December 31, 2025 liquidity: 869.356 plus 106.6 equals 975.956; decline 304.428. 3. Debt movement (US$m, carrying amounts, Q3 statements page:11): 1,985.426 less 1,275.052 equals 710.374. Instrument changes: revolver +321.628; overrun facility +68.130; Sprott facility +355.548 less its redemption option derivative asset 42.495 equals +313.053; equipment facility +35.296; government contributions +2.126; senior notes +0.213; senior notes redemption option derivative asset change +10.543 (from a deduction of 14.703 to 4.160); Commercial Loan Facility minus 15.940; RRF Facility minus 4.237; VAT Facility minus 20.438. These sum to 710.374. Foran-related debt is 313.053 + 35.296 + 2.126 = 350.475, which equals the Canada segment debt of 350.475 (Q3 statements page:28). 4. Remaining Skouries capital per the release (US$m): project capital estimate 1,425 less cumulative project capital invested to September 30, 2026 of 1,379 equals 46; accelerated operational capital estimate 390 less cumulative 285.6 equals 104.4; total 150.4, with up to 30 more depending on timing of commercial production (Q3 release pages:5, 8). Estimates are stated as approximate. 5. Illustrative leverage and interest cover are carried unchanged from CP-1 (1.67x and 1.34x on annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA; 11.96x and 9.81x cash interest cover). They are not repeated as new calculations and not trailing or covenant measures. 6. Distributions: dividends paid 54.103 plus shares cancelled 83.895 equals 137.998 (US$m), carried from CP-1A.

rows.label: Eldorado has profitable operating mines and reasonable reported leverage on an illustrative basis, but is spending far more than it earns while two projects start up. The credit view is cautiously constructive and depends on those start-ups.
Debt rose and cash fell sharply over nine months, so liquidity declined, while the nine-month cash shortfall after capital spending was large.
Illustrative leverage and cash interest cover look comfortable, but neither is a trailing or covenant figure.
Skouries and McIlvenna Bay are not yet in commercial production, and cost estimates and production guidance have moved against the company.
Maturities are concentrated in one year window, when the notes and revolver both fall due, and the project loan starts repaying in December 2026.
Start-up delay or further cost overrun at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay

### Financial base view

The financial base at September 30, 2026 is one of strong reported profitability alongside heavy investment and rising leverage. Nine-month 2026 revenue is above the prior year because the average realised gold price is higher, while gold sold is lower (the release attributes the revenue increase to price, partly offset by volume), and Adjusted EBITDA is also higher. At the same time, cash capital spending, including capitalised interest, exceeds operating cash flow, so cash has fallen and debt has risen, partly through the Foran acquisition (debt assumed) and partly through revolver draws. The base is usable for a snapshot with these limits: trailing (LTM) EBITDA and so trailing leverage are not supplied because FY2025 full-year figures are absent; interest cover is shown on matched nine-month and quarter bases only; and covenant headroom cannot be computed because the covenant definitions and issuer-reported ratios are not supplied. The September 30, 2026 balance sheet also includes the Foran acquisition on a provisional fair-value basis, and Skouries and McIlvenna Bay are not yet in commercial production, so period earnings do not yet carry their full contribution while debt and interest do.

## Calculations

All inputs are printed in the cited sources; results are calculated here, not printed. Q3 statements means 6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-30_unauditedcondensedconsolid.htm.jsonl and Q3 release the Q3 2026 earnings release.

1. Total debt at September 30, 2026: 148,472 current plus 1,836,954 non-current equals 1,985,426 (US$ thousand), which matches the printed debt note total. The movement from December 31, 2025 is 1,985,426 less 1,275,052 equals 710,374, which equals the sum of instrument-level changes in the debt note.

2. Net debt at September 30, 2026: 1,985,426 less unrestricted cash 396,828 equals 1,588,598. If restricted cash of 71,898 is also deducted, 1,516,700. Net debt at December 31, 2025: 1,275,052 less 869,356 equals 405,696 (no restricted cash was held then).

3. Illustrative leverage (not LTM): Adjusted EBITDA nine months 2026 of 892.0 times 4/3 equals 1,189.3 (US$m). Total debt 1,985.426 divided by 1,189.3 equals 1.67x. Net debt 1,588.598 divided by 1,189.3 equals 1.34x. The method is a straight-line scale-up and is not a trailing twelve-month figure; no figure is stated for LTM because FY2025 EBITDA is not supplied.

4. Interest cover (US$m): Q3 2026 275.2 / (13.165 + 14.879 = 28.044) equals 9.81x. Nine months 2026 892.0 / (28.611 + 45.943 = 74.554) equals 11.96x. Q3 2025 196.3 / (9.174 + 8.437 = 17.611) equals 11.15x. Nine months 2025 571.1 / (19.601 + 28.457 = 48.058) equals 11.88x. Excluding capitalised interest paid, nine months 2026 is 892.0 / 28.611 equals 31.18x. Cash interest here is cash paid on debt: interest paid in financing activities plus capitalised interest paid in investing activities. Adjusted EBITDA is the company's non-IFRS measure.

5. Liquidity at September 30, 2026: 396.828 plus 274.7 equals 671.528 (US$m). At June 30, 2026: 554.562 plus 300.0 equals 854.562. At March 31, 2026: 629.724 plus 158.1 equals 787.824. At December 31, 2025: 869.356 plus 106.6 equals 975.956. Restricted cash is excluded in every period. The printed available balance was used rather than facility limit less drawn amount: at September 30, 2026 600.0 less 325.0 equals 275.0 against 274.7 printed; the 0.3 difference is not explained in the sources.

6. Debt maturity buckets (US$m): sum of the Q3 commitments table rows by column, plus 500.0 senior notes in year 3. Year 1: 0 + 115.532 + 15.628 + 9.242 + 0.651 = 141.053. Year 2: 100.887 + 31.255 + 9.816 + 0.589 = 142.547. Year 3: 325.000 + 92.480 + 31.255 + 10.060 + 500.0 = 958.795. Year 4: 126.109 + 31.255 + 5.082 = 162.446. Year 5: 168.145 + 185.467 + 1.113 = 354.725. Over 5 years: 252.217 + 5.959 = 258.176. Total 2,017.742 versus the sum of principal amounts 500.0 + 325.0 + 855.369 + 294.860 + 35.313 + 7.199 = 2,017.741 (rounding). The principal total exceeds the carrying total of 1,985.426 because carrying amounts are net of unamortised fees and redemption option derivative assets and, for government contributions, discounted. Bucket years are measured from the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date; the table's own bucket definition is assumed to run from that date.

7. Cash flow gap, nine months 2026 (US$ thousand): operating cash flow 425,747 less additions to property, plant and equipment 1,210,017 less capitalised interest paid 45,943 equals negative 830,213 before acquisitions, financing and dividends. The company-defined free cash flow is negative 654.3 (US$m); the difference reflects the company's own definition (non-IFRS) and is not reconciled here.
8. Cash movement check: opening cash 869,356 less net decrease 472,528 equals closing 396,828, matching the cash flow statement.

9. Income statement checks: earnings from mine operations 253,317 less the expense block below it (exploration 17,116, standby 6,318, general and administrative 11,177, share-based payments 3,763, write-down 1,569, foreign exchange gain 4,029, acquisition costs 89, net 36,003) equals earnings from operations 217,314 for Q3 2026. For nine months 2026: 791,963 less 86,812 equals 705,151. Earnings from operations plus other income 5,613 less finance costs 13,531 equals pre-tax earnings 209,396 for Q3 2026; nine months 2026 705,151 plus 15,821 less 37,660 equals 683,312. All match the printed totals.

10. Effective tax rate on continuing operations, nine months 2026: 257,114 / 683,312 equals 37.6%. Nine months 2025: 54,604 / 324,573 equals 16.8%, which includes a deferred tax recovery of 89,390 (note 12). The two rates are not comparable without that item.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Eldorado is a three-country gold and base metals producer in the middle of two large project start-ups, after buying Foran for shares in April 2026. Project costs and delays are rising while debt has increased. | Medium | The annual information form, ownership detail and acquisition agreements are not in the pack, so ownership and legal protections cannot be assessed. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Skouries and McIlvenna Bay both produced first concentrate in 2026 but neither is in commercial production, and the Skouries capital estimate has risen. | Cash needs stay high until commercial production is reached, so the credit rests on the operating mines and the start-ups meeting their dates. | Medium |

| Foran was bought for shares and brought acquired debt, including a secured credit facility with a company guarantee. | Equity paid for the deal, which limits new borrowing, but the acquired lender has security over the acquired assets. | High |

| The 2026 production outlook has been cut while costs have been raised, and a dividend programme started and buybacks continued alongside heavy project spending. | Lower volumes and returns to shareholders both weigh on cash generation; no creditor-adverse actions are documented. | Medium |

| Revenue is concentrated in gold and in three countries, with Canada the largest segment in the first nine months of 2026. | Country and metal price exposure drives revenue visibility; the sources give no customer concentration data. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Eldorado's business is a producing gold group with polymetallic by-products, now adding two copper-bearing mines through commissioning at the same time. Revenue in the first nine months of 2026 came mainly from gold, in three geographic segments, with Canada the largest after the Foran acquisition. The operating mines carry the credit today: Lamaque and Olympias improved, while Kisladag and Efemcukuru weakened on lower grades, and cost guidance was raised. The transaction that matters to a creditor is the all-share purchase of Foran, which closed on April 14, 2026: it added McIlvenna Bay and debt assumed of 355,321 (US$ thousand, recorded at fair value), mainly the Sprott facility, which is secured on the acquired assets with a company guarantee, plus an equipment facility. No new notes were issued in the period; new funding was revolver draws, the final overrun draw on the Skouries project loan and the acquired debt. Management describes Skouries as fully funded; that is a management claim, and the pack does not include a funding model. Skouries first concentrate was achieved on September 8, 2026 and McIlvenna Bay first copper concentrate in June 2026, but both commercial production dates are late in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the capital estimates and 2026 production guidance have moved adversely. Ownership, control rights and any shareholder agreements are not disclosed in the pack. Behaviour is assessed on documented actions only: a dividend programme was started and buybacks continued during the build, leadership changed on September 30, 2026, and no priming, drop-down or other creditor-adverse action is documented. Source evidence is primary and dated, so evidence quality is High for filed statements and Medium for management releases.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one transaction in the period is the acquisition of Foran Mining Corporation, completed on April 14, 2026 by court-approved plan of arrangement. The Q3 statements say the Company acquired 100% of the issued and outstanding common shares of Foran for 0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran share (Q3 statements page:8: "0.1128 Eldorado common shares and C$0.01 in cash for each Foran common share"). Total consideration transferred was 2,394,995 (US$ thousand), of which share consideration was 2,385,625, cash 4,154, replacement option value 3,096 and the previously held equity interest 2,120; 64,668,321 shares were issued (Q3 statements pages:8, 17). The principal asset is the McIlvenna Bay project in Saskatchewan. The acquisition was therefore financed with equity, not debt, and the statements show net cash received on acquisition of 159,110 (Q3 statements page:3). Net assets acquired include property, plant and equipment of 2,696,191, goodwill of 446,181, debt assumed of 355,321 and a deferred tax liability of 501,024; the measurement is preliminary and may be adjusted for up to one year (Q3 statements pages:9, 10). Acquisition-related costs expensed in the nine months were 19.3 million (US$) (Q3 statements page:10). The Q1 statements disclose the completion as an event after the reporting date (Q1 statements page:22).

The debt assumed comprises the Sprott Credit Facility (a fully drawn 250 million non-revolving facility plus 44.9 million capitalised interest, maturing September 30, 2031, floating at 6.95% over the greater of three-month SOFR and 2.00%, secured by the realisable value of the acquired Foran assets and subject to a Company guarantee), the Sandvik Equipment Finance Facility (C$50.1 million outstanding, 60-month repayment) and repayable government contributions (Q3 statements pages:14, 15). Principal repayments on the Sprott facility start on June 30, 2027 at 2.65% of outstanding principal per quarter. Its terms mean the lender has a claim over the acquired assets ahead of unsecured creditors of the group on those assets, and the Company guarantee ties the facility to the parent; the pack does not include the credit agreement, so the full security and guarantee scope is Insufficient Information.

No new bond or note issue is reported in the period. New borrowing was: draws on the revolving senior secured credit facility totalling 325.0 million in the nine months (225.0 million of it in Q3 2026); the final 60.0 million euro draw on the Skouries Contingent Overrun Facility in Q2 2026; and net proceeds of 2,469 (US$ thousand) from other debt. The revolver was increased from 350 million to 450 million on May 26, 2026 through the accordion, and on August 12, 2026 amended to a 600 million limit with maturity extended to March 1, 2029 and, in the Company's words, improved pricing and covenant terms (Q3 statements page:14: "enhancing financial flexibility through improved pricing and covenant terms"). The amended covenant terms are not stated beyond the interest cover and net leverage levels in the note, so what changed is Insufficient Information. The equity commitment letter of credit under the revolver for Skouries was reduced to nil as the equity funding was completed in Q3 2026 (Q3 statements page:14), which releases revolver capacity; at September 30, 2026 the revolver availability was 274.7 million (Q3 statements page:14).

Distributions during the build: the Company initiated a quarterly dividend programme with the first payment on March 13, 2026 (Q1 release page:2), paid 54.1 million of dividends in the nine months, bought back and cancelled 2,419,992 shares for 83.9 million and bought a further 240,000 shares for 8.7 million held in trust (Q3 statements page:18), and declared a fourth quarter dividend of 0.075 per share on October 28, 2026 (Q3 statements page:18). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company states compliance (Q3 statements page:11). Mechanically, these distributions total about 138.0 million for dividends and cancelled buybacks in nine months 2026 while company-defined free cash flow was negative 654.3 million (CP-1), so they were funded from cash and borrowings. This is an Analyst Interpretation of capital allocation, not a finding of extraction: the covenant tests are met per the Company, and no related-party leakage or collateral release is documented.

Subsequent events to the cutoff: the fourth quarter dividend declaration of October 28, 2026 is the only post-quarter event in the pack. Nothing dated after October 28, 2026 is supplied, so developments between that date and November 5, 2026 are Insufficient Information.

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability and margin. Evidence: realised price up from 3,527 to 4,326 per ounce (US$) while ounces sold fell and AISC rose (Q3 release pages:14, 15). Mechanic: revenue is carrying lower volumes at higher cost, so margin per ounce is more sensitive to the gold price than a year ago. Implication: debt service capacity rests on gold staying near current levels until the new mines add volume; the Skouries and McIlvenna Bay start-ups are the offset, and they are not yet in commercial production. Countering evidence: Lamaque output rose and Olympias costs per ounce fell (Q3 release pages:19, 21).

2. Cash conversion and refinancing. Evidence: acquired debt, revolver draws and a larger project capital estimate (Q3 statements page:14; Q3 release page:7). Mechanic: cash needs continue until commercial production, funded by the revolver and the cash balance; the Term Facility begins amortising on December 31, 2026 (Q3 statements page:13). Implication: refinancing and liquidity are the pressure points; the senior notes and the revolver both mature in the third year bucket (CP-1). Counter: equity paid for Foran and the revolver was extended to March 1, 2029.

3. Concentration. Evidence: Canada, Turkiye and Greece segments; Greece carries the Skouries project and the Term Facility secured on Skouries and Hellas Gold assets (Q3 statements pages:12, 16). Mechanic: the non-recourse project loan keeps Skouries debt away from the parent but ring-fences the cash flows of the Greek assets for that lender; the revolver and notes sit with the rest of the group. Implication: creditor claims on Greek cash flows differ by instrument; the pack does not contain the intercreditor terms, so recovery or ranking is not assessed.

4. Sponsor alignment and distributions. Evidence: dividends and buybacks during heavy spending (Q3 statements page:18). Mechanic: shareholder returns draw on the same cash as project funding. Implication: a monitoring point; no creditor-adverse action is documented. Counter: the Foran purchase was equity-funded.
5. Key uncertainties: commercial production timing and cost at both start-ups; covenant headroom (not supplied); ownership; Foran fair values (preliminary).
### Conflicts

No conflicting statements were found between the supplied documents. Dated revisions are logged, not conflicts, and neither value is chosen over the other: the Skouries total project capital estimate was approximately 1.315 billion in the Q1 release and approximately 1.425 billion in the Q3 release; the McIlvenna Bay project capital estimate was 952 million in the Q2 release and 975 million in the Q3 release; the 2026 production outlook was 490,000 to 590,000 ounces in the Q1 release and 425,000 to 475,000 ounces in the Q3 release, on different perimeters because the Q1 outlook preceded Foran. Each is a later update to the earlier figure.

1. Geographic revenue shares, nine months 2026 (US$ thousand): Turkiye 555,587 / 1,531,744 equals 36.3%; Canada 692,340 / 1,531,744 equals 45.2%; Greece 283,817 / 1,531,744 equals 18.5%. Canada includes McIlvenna Bay revenue of 9.6 million since acquisition.

2. Gold share of revenue from contracts with customers, nine months 2026: gold doré 1,000,604 plus gold concentrate 432,488 equals 1,433,092; divided by 1,564,476 (revenue from contracts with customers before provisional pricing adjustments) equals 91.6%. Source: Q3 statements page:16. Silver, lead, zinc and copper make up the rest.
3. Foran share issue relative to shares outstanding: 64,668,321 / 261,556,941 equals 24.7%.

4. Foran consideration check: 64,668,321 shares at 36.89 per share equals about 2,385.6 million, matching share consideration of 2,385,625 (US$ thousand). Total 2,385,625 plus 4,154 plus 3,096 plus 2,120 equals 2,394,995, matching total consideration. Net assets acquired equal consideration (2,394,995) in the statements.
5. Net cash from the acquisition: cash acquired 163,264 less cash consideration 4,154 equals 159,110 (US$ thousand), matching the cash flow statement.

6. Shareholder distributions, nine months 2026 (US$ thousand): dividends paid 54,103 plus shares purchased for cancellation 83,895 equals 137,998; including shares held in trust for restricted share units of 8,683 gives 146,681. Compare company-defined free cash flow of negative 654.3 million for the same period (CP-1, Q3 release page:13).

7. Project capital estimate movements: Skouries 1.425 billion less 1.315 billion equals 110 million, which the release itemises as 65 million of project costs plus 45 million moved from later growth capital (Q3 release page:7). McIlvenna Bay 975 million less 952 million equals 23 million, matching the release ("approximately $23 million").

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Eldorado has profitable operating mines and reasonable reported leverage on an illustrative basis, but is spending far more than it earns while two projects start up. The credit view is cautiously constructive and depends on those start-ups. | Medium | Trailing earnings, covenant headroom and ownership cannot be established because full-year 2025 statements and legal documents are not in the pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt rose and cash fell sharply over nine months, so liquidity declined, while the nine-month cash shortfall after capital spending was large. | Liquidity is adequate against near maturities but is being consumed until the projects generate cash. | High |
| Illustrative leverage and cash interest cover look comfortable, but neither is a trailing or covenant figure. | Headroom against the revolver covenants cannot be confirmed. | Medium |

| Skouries and McIlvenna Bay are not yet in commercial production, and cost estimates and production guidance have moved against the company. | Further slippage would extend the cash drain and delay deleveraging. | Medium |

| Maturities are concentrated in one year window, when the notes and revolver both fall due, and the project loan starts repaying in December 2026. | Refinancing capacity matters most for the third year. | Medium |
### Credit view

Eldorado Gold's credit view is cautiously constructive: profitable mines at high gold prices support debt, but debt is rising and cash falling while two new mines are commissioned. The strongest support is operating earnings and low illustrative leverage, financed partly by shares issued for Foran. The weakest point is nine-month free cash flow of USD negative 654.3 million and liquidity down from USD 976.0 million to USD 671.5 million since December 2025. The outcome depends on Skouries and McIlvenna Bay reaching commercial production in late Q4 2026 at or near the revised budgets, on gold prices holding, and on the senior notes and revolver refinancing from 2029. Confidence is Medium because trailing earnings and covenant headroom are not supplied.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | Assessment | Tag | Basis |
| Overall | Cautiously constructive, Medium confidence | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 financial base; CP-1A business and transaction view |
| Business risk | Moderate; diversified across three countries and metals but exposed to gold price and two start-ups | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1A company and operating model, project status |
| Financial risk | Moderate and rising; debt up, free cash flow negative | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 leverage, free cash flow and cash flow gap |
| Liquidity | Adequate for near-term maturities, thinner than at December 2025 | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 liquidity table and maturity buckets |
| Governance and creditor control | No creditor-adverse action documented; ownership and legal protections not assessable | Insufficient Information | CP-1A governance table, gaps G16 and G18 |
### Key findings

1. Eldorado Gold's cash is being consumed by growth spending rather than by operations. In the nine months to September 30, 2026 it generated USD 425.7 million of operating cash flow from continuing operations but spent USD 1,210.0 million on property, plant and equipment and USD 45.9 million on capitalised interest paid, a shortfall of about USD 830.2 million before acquisition cash, dividends, buybacks and borrowings (CP-1, Calculations). Company-defined free cash flow was negative USD 654.3 million; excluding Skouries and McIlvenna Bay it was positive USD 202.1 million (Q3 release page:13). Mechanic: the operating mines are cash generative and the two projects absorb it, so default risk is driven by project completion, not by the operating base. Documentary Fact.

2. Liquidity has fallen but covers near-term maturities. Unrestricted cash was USD 396.8 million and the undrawn revolver USD 274.7 million at September 30, 2026, together USD 671.5 million against USD 976.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1). Principal falling due within a year is USD 141.1 million, so liquidity is about 4.8 times that amount (Calculations). Restricted cash of USD 71.9 million for the Skouries term loan reserve and the undrawn euro 30 million VAT facility are excluded. Mechanic: the cushion is adequate for scheduled repayments but not for a prolonged slip in the start-ups combined with a lower gold price. Analyst Interpretation.

3. Debt rose by USD 710.4 million to USD 1,985.4 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026 (carrying amount). The increase came from USD 321.6 million of revolver borrowings, USD 68.1 million from the final overrun draw on the Skouries loan, and USD 350.5 million of Foran-related debt (the Sprott facility net of its redemption option derivative asset, the equipment facility and government contributions), partly offset by repayments and movements on the Skouries project loans and the VAT facility (CP-1 debt table; Calculations). Foran itself was paid for with shares (USD 2,385.6 million of share consideration), which kept the acquisition from adding to leverage through the purchase price (CP-1A). Documentary Fact.

4. Reported leverage looks moderate only on an illustrative basis. Total debt to annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA is 1.67 times and net debt to the same measure 1.34 times; neither is a trailing twelve-month figure because FY2025 EBITDA is not supplied, and the base includes Foran only from April 14, 2026 and no Skouries contribution (CP-1). Cash interest cover (Adjusted EBITDA over interest paid plus capitalised interest paid) was 11.96 times for nine months 2026 and 9.81 times for Q3 2026. These do not use the covenant definitions, so headroom against the revolver tests of at least 3.00 times interest cover and at most 3.50 times net leverage is Not calculable. The illustrative figures sit well inside those levels, which is a reading and not a compliance finding; the Company states it complied at September 30, 2026 (Q3 statements page:14). Analyst Interpretation.

5. Skouries and McIlvenna Bay execution is the pivotal risk. First concentrate was reached at Skouries on September 8, 2026 and at McIlvenna Bay in June 2026, with commercial production for both expected late in Q4 2026 (CP-1A). The Skouries project capital estimate rose from about USD 1.315 billion in the Q1 release to about USD 1.425 billion, the McIlvenna Bay estimate from USD 952 million in the Q2 release to USD 975 million, and the 2026 production outlook was cut to 425,000 to 475,000 ounces from 495,000 to 600,000 ounces. On the release's own figures, remaining Skouries project capital is about USD 46 million and accelerated operational capital about USD 104 million, with up to USD 30 million more possible (Calculations); the remaining McIlvenna Bay spend is Not calculable because spending before the acquisition date is not in the pack. Mechanic: further slippage extends the period of negative free cash flow and delays the debt reduction that management says it expects. Management Language on funding ("fully funded") is not adopted because no funding model is supplied.

6. Refinancing is concentrated and amortisation starts soon. Principal due by year after September 30, 2026 is USD 141.1 million, 142.5 million, 958.8 million, 162.4 million, 354.7 million and 258.2 million beyond year five (CP-1). The third year contains the USD 500.0 million 6.25% senior notes due September 1, 2029 and the USD 325.0 million revolver drawn to March 1, 2029, the largest bucket by a wide margin. The Skouries term loan, non-recourse to the parent and secured on the Skouries and Hellas Gold assets, begins repaying on December 31, 2026 in 13 semi-annual instalments (Q3 statements page:13). Mechanic: if the start-ups deliver, cash flow and the equity-funded balance sheet should support refinancing; if not, the 2029 wall arrives with higher debt. Documentary Fact for the schedule, Analyst Interpretation for the refinancing reading.

7. Shareholder returns continued during the build. Dividends of USD 54.1 million and cancelled buybacks of USD 83.9 million in nine months 2026, about USD 138.0 million together, were paid while free cash flow was negative (CP-1A, Calculations). The senior notes restrict distributions in certain circumstances and the Company reports compliance. No creditor-adverse action is documented. Mechanic: these returns draw on the same liquidity that funds the projects and can be reduced by the board; they are a monitoring point, not a finding of extraction. Analyst Interpretation.

8. Earnings quality needs care. Net earnings from continuing operations were USD 426.2 million for nine months 2026 against USD 270.0 million a year earlier, but the 2025 period included a deferred tax recovery of USD 89.4 million and the 2026 effective tax rate was 37.6% against 16.8% (CP-1 Calculations). The Adjusted EBITDA measure of USD 892.0 million adds back a USD 97.6 million realised loss on gold and copper derivatives and USD 21.3 million of acquisition costs, and removes a USD 100.6 million unrealised derivative gain (Q3 release page:24). Mechanic: the realised swap loss is a real cost of the Skouries financing hedges that the adjusted figure leaves out; those swaps have expired with financial settlement (Q3 statements page:22), so the item should not recur, but the adjusted measure is higher than the unadjusted result for 2026. Documentary Fact.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, the operating base earns at high gold prices: the average realised gold price was USD 4,326 per ounce in Q3 2026 against USD 3,527 a year earlier, and Adjusted EBITDA for nine months 2026 was USD 892.0 million against USD 571.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1). Second, diversification across Turkiye, Canada and Greece with Canada now the largest segment at about 45% of nine-month revenue, and several mines at different cost levels, with Lamaque cash costs of USD 897 per ounce in Q3 2026 (CP-1A, Calculations; Analyst Interpretation). Third, an equity-funded Foran purchase that added roughly 24.7% to shares outstanding rather than debt to fund the price, and an extended and enlarged revolver of USD 600.0 million maturing March 1, 2029 (Documentary Fact). Fourth, a Skouries project loan that the notes describe as non-recourse to Eldorado Gold Corporation, which limits parent exposure to that lender if the project falls short (Documentary Fact for the description; the legal documents are not supplied, so the extent of recourse is not verified). Fifth, interest cover on cash interest of about ten to twelve times on matched bases (Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure).

Weaknesses. First, negative free cash flow and falling liquidity, with debt up USD 710.4 million in nine months (Documentary Fact). Second, cost and guidance deterioration: all-in sustaining cost guidance raised and 2026 production outlook cut, with Kisladag and Olympias weaker (Documentary Fact). Third, start-up risk and rising project capital at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay, with commercial production dates still forward-looking (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Fourth, a concentrated maturity profile and the start of Skouries term loan repayments in December 2026 (Documentary Fact). Fifth, a leadership transition on September 30, 2026 during the overrun period and shareholder distributions during the build (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the credit effect). Sixth, high effective tax in 2026 and exposure to a high gold price: the earnings strength depends on a gold price the company does not control, and the pack contains no sensitivity (Analyst Interpretation; sensitivity Not supplied).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Start-up delay or further cost overrun at Skouries and McIlvenna Bay | Longer period of capital spending and negative free cash flow, lower 2026 and 2027 volumes | Draws on cash and revolver; delays deleveraging | Material |

| Gold price decline | Revenue is price driven while unit costs and royalties rise with price and volumes fall | Cuts cash generation of the operating mines that fund the projects and service debt | Material |

| Refinancing of 2029 maturities | Senior notes and revolver fall in the same year bucket, after the Skouries loan has begun amortising | Depends on start-up success and market access; no market pricing in the pack | Material |
| Covenant headroom unknown | Revolver tests on interest cover and net leverage use definitions not supplied; Term Facility tests not stated | Cannot confirm distance to default triggers | Material |
| Shareholder distributions during the build | Dividends and buybacks use the same cash as project funding | Reduces liquidity buffer if projects slip | Minor |

| Ownership and creditor-control terms unknown | No ownership data; executed documents not supplied | Cannot assess change of control, priming capacity or guarantor structure beyond summaries | Minor |
| Provisional Foran accounting | Fair values may change within the year | Goodwill and acquired debt carrying values may move | Minor |
## Calculations

1. Nine-month 2026 cash shortfall after capital spending (US$ thousand): 425,747 operating cash flow less 1,210,017 property, plant and equipment additions less 45,943 capitalised interest paid equals negative 830,213 (inputs from CP-1; checked to Q3 statements pages:3). It excludes the 159,110 of cash received on the Foran acquisition, dividends, buybacks and borrowings.

2. Liquidity cover of year-one maturities (US$m): cash 396.828 plus undrawn revolver 274.7 equals 671.528; divided by principal due within one year 141.053 equals 4.76 times. December 31, 2025 liquidity: 869.356 plus 106.6 equals 975.956; decline 304.428.

3. Debt movement (US$m, carrying amounts, Q3 statements page:11): 1,985.426 less 1,275.052 equals 710.374. Instrument changes: revolver +321.628; overrun facility +68.130; Sprott facility +355.548 less its redemption option derivative asset 42.495 equals +313.053; equipment facility +35.296; government contributions +2.126; senior notes +0.213; senior notes redemption option derivative asset change +10.543 (from a deduction of 14.703 to 4.160); Commercial Loan Facility minus 15.940; RRF Facility minus 4.237; VAT Facility minus 20.438. These sum to 710.374. Foran-related debt is 313.053 + 35.296 + 2.126 = 350.475, which equals the Canada segment debt of 350.475 (Q3 statements page:28).

4. Remaining Skouries capital per the release (US$m): project capital estimate 1,425 less cumulative project capital invested to September 30, 2026 of 1,379 equals 46; accelerated operational capital estimate 390 less cumulative 285.6 equals 104.4; total 150.4, with up to 30 more depending on timing of commercial production (Q3 release pages:5, 8). Estimates are stated as approximate.

5. Illustrative leverage and interest cover are carried unchanged from CP-1 (1.67x and 1.34x on annualised nine-month Adjusted EBITDA; 11.96x and 9.81x cash interest cover). They are not repeated as new calculations and not trailing or covenant measures.
6. Distributions: dividends paid 54.103 plus shares cancelled 83.895 equals 137.998 (US$m), carried from CP-1A.
## Gaps
| ID | Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Severity | Action |

| G1 | Audited FY2025 statements, FY2025 EBITDA and cash flow not supplied (CP-0 G1) | No trailing leverage or cover; no full-year trend; restricts every leverage conclusion | High | Obtain the FY2025 annual report exhibits |
| G2 | Management discussion not supplied (CP-0 G2) | Liquidity discussion, undrawn VAT facility, capital commitments and funding plan unavailable | Medium | Obtain MD&A |
| G5 | Covenant definitions, Term Facility covenant levels and issuer-reported ratios not supplied | Headroom Not calculable | High | Obtain credit agreements and compliance disclosure |
| G6 | Foran allocation provisional | Debt and goodwill may change | Medium | Track measurement period updates |
| G16 | Ownership and control not disclosed | Governance, change-of-control and alignment not assessable | Medium | Obtain annual information form |
| G18 | Executed debt documents not supplied | Security, guarantee, ranking and intercreditor terms known only from summaries; no recovery conclusion is possible | Medium | Obtain documents |
| G22 | Funding model for project completion not supplied | The "fully funded" claim untestable; remaining McIlvenna Bay spend Not calculable | Medium | Obtain MD&A liquidity section |

| G23 | No sensitivity of earnings or cash flow to the gold price, and no hedging detail beyond the derivatives listed in the statements | Downside cases cannot be sized from the pack | Medium | Obtain MD&A or investor materials |
| G24 | No market pricing for debt other than the senior notes fair value; no ratings in the context | No market-implied view; ratings Not supplied | Low | Not required for this snapshot |
| G25 | Events after October 28, 2026 up to the November 5, 2026 cutoff not covered | Possible later developments unseen | Low | Check later filings |
CP-1A readiness judgment for CP-2 was READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, so the confidence in the assessment is below High.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validator). CP-5 should trace the figures in this handoff to CP-1 and the filings, check that Management Language rows are not treated as filed fact, and confirm that gaps G1, G2, G5, G6, G16, G18, G22 and G23 stay open. Consistency note for the trace: CP-1A quotes debt assumed at the acquisition date of USD 355.3 million at fair value; this handoff uses the September 30, 2026 carrying amount of Foran-related debt, USD 350.5 million net of the Sprott redemption option derivative asset. Both are correct for their dates and are not a conflict.
